title: AFO musicians' corporation
summary: He describes the All For One group's aim to let session musicians share success and says he was only a member by proxy.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: After you got out of the Army, didn't the All For One group get together with Harold and Batiste? Was that pretty soon after that?
After, after. Yeah. I don't know whether it was, I think it was a little before.
What was the philosophy behind AFO was to have like musicians produce themselves and control their distribution? What was the philosophy behind that? Behind what? Behind the AFO.

There were certain musicians making a lot of sessions and playing on a lot of hit records. And they thought they would form a corporation of mainly them, which was a very good idea. And I think that's what it was about. Just that they would reap some benefits of whatever success they could be responsible for. And they were fairly involved in that group? Very fairly for a little while. Not very much.
Okay. I think that's been overstated in several accounts I've read about you.

Well, we never, I never made any moves with them or got anything going on. I definitely agreed with them. And I was sort of like a member by proxy sort of. But never really got together with them. I did anything.
Do you think that idea was almost too advanced for a lot of musicians to work?
Oh no. Oh no. The idea of it was business and business is over. So I don't think it was too advanced.
Do you think it could be, it could be done today then? Oh yeah. Some people got together.

It could be done. It could be done. I don't know if it, if it would be for the best interests of people because being a good businessman is important and being a good musician is. And if you're going to really develop your instrument, I don't know how much you develop your business skills along with it. You can do both. But for a whole group of people, it would be over average of being fortunate to find eight or ten men who can play and will do business together, actual business on an equal level. That's just very hard.
